cover.headline: A real recovery in a capital-heavy business; its own EV/EBITDA history says there is upside, its cash flows say be careful
cover.lead: Piramal Pharma runs three businesses: a global contract development and manufacturing business (CDMO, 55% of FY26 revenue of ₹8,869 cr), hospital generics led by inhaled anaesthetics (CHG, 30%) and Indian consumer brands (PCH, 15%), plus 49% of an ophthalmology JV with AbbVie. FY26 was a bad year: revenue −3%, a ₹326 cr loss, as one large on-patent CDMO customer stopped ordering to use up stock. Q1FY27 turned: revenue +17% (about 9-10 points from the rupee), EBITDA +72%, guidance of early-to-mid-teens growth kept. The stock rose ~19% in 2026 to ₹207 on 30-Sep-2026. Most brokers value it on a **sum of the parts built on EV/EBITDA** (Motilal Oswal, ICICI Direct; Choice and InCred on one consolidated EV/EBITDA); profits are too small for P/E. Piramal reports one segment, so we value the three businesses together at **21x Sep-28E EBITDA** (its own one-year-forward median since May-2023, 20.0x, × the pharma peers' +5.1% move), add the AbbVie JV at 10x its profit share and deduct net debt: **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}); we initiate with BUY**. Cross-checks are far lower: P/E ₹119, DCF ₹98. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Every business grew 15-19% in Q1FY27, CDMO for the first time in five quarters, on better biotech funding, more RFPs and a bigger sales team. We forecast revenue +15.3% / +11.9% / +10.7% and an EBITDA margin rising from 10.4% to 13.0% / 15.5% / 17.1% (FY27-29E), below ICICI Direct's 16.4% / 17.9%.

arguments.h: But EBITDA is not profit here
arguments.p: Depreciation (~₹1,000 cr), interest (~₹400 cr) and a tax bill that runs ahead of profit (overseas losses earn no credit) absorb most of EBITDA: we forecast EPS of ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.2|n1}} for FY27-29E. At ₹207 that is 89.0x FY28E earnings. The DCF (₹98; ₹156 with a 25% tax rate and 25% margins) does not support the price.

arguments.h: The upside rests on the multiple, not on our estimates
arguments.p: Our EBITDA is below the bulls', yet our target is above theirs because Piramal's own forward EV/EBITDA median (20.0x since May-2023, every weekly point: FY26 EBITDA fell 36%, not below half its peak, so the EBITDA trough test excludes nothing) is higher than the street's blended segment multiples (₹220-230 on our numbers). That median includes Apr-24 to Mar-25, when the multiple reached ~33x on collapsing EBITDA; leaving those dates out (the EPS reading of the trough rule) gives 16x and ₹205.

Conversion of RFPs into orders at the under-used US and UK sites (the margin lever); Kenalog and ex-US sevoflurane in CHG; and supply: Carlyle (CA Alchemy, ~18%) has twice tried to sell and stopped. Net debt (₹4,140 cr) is above CARE's 3.5x trigger and rises in FY27.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first Kenalog quarter, CDMO order conversion, and a possible guidance upgrade (management said it would revisit after the September quarter).
Lexington sterile fill-finish expansion (H2 CY2027) and ADC orders at Riverview and Grangemouth; any return of the destocked on-patent product (not in FY27 guidance).
Carlyle (CA Alchemy, 17.95%): a block sale was planned and called off in August 2026; a completed sale would add supply but remove the overhang.
US tariff and trade terms for India-made innovator work (generics are excluded; US and UK plants are not affected).
CARE's leverage trigger (net debt/PBILDT 3.5x): a downgrade risk if FY27 EBITDA disappoints.

sections.title: Three businesses under one roof: a global CDMO, a niche hospital-generics franchise and Indian consumer brands

blocks.p: Piramal Pharma was carved out of Piramal Enterprises and listed on 19-Oct-2022. It has three businesses that share little beyond the name and a balance sheet. **CDMO** (Piramal Pharma Solutions, ₹4,915 cr in FY26, 55% of business revenue) develops and manufactures drugs for ~500 pharma and biotech customers at 15 sites in India, the US, Canada and the UK: drug substances (APIs) including high-potency ones, peptides, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and sterile injectables. About 47% of its revenue comes from innovation-related work (development, discovery and on-patent commercial supply); the other 53% is commercial supply of older products. **Complex Hospital Generics** (Piramal Critical Care, ₹2,703 cr, 30%) sells inhaled anaesthetics (sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane; 64% of CHG), intrathecal baclofen and morphine for spasticity and pain (15%), injectable pain products (11%) and others to 6,000+ hospitals in 100+ countries; half of it is sold in the US. **Consumer Healthcare** (PCH, ₹1,274 cr, 14%) sells over-the-counter brands in India: Little's (baby care), Lacto Calamine (skin), i-pill and i-range (women's health), Saridon, Polycrol, Tetmosol, CIR.

On top of the three, Piramal owns **49% of AbbVie Therapeutics India**, which sells AbbVie's eye-care brands (Lumigan, Combigan, Alphagan, Refresh Tears, Pred Forte) in India: revenue ₹510 cr and profit ₹123 cr in FY26, ₹60 cr of it Piramal's share. It sits below EBITDA, in "share of associates". It also owns **33.33% of Yapan Bio**, a small loss-making vaccines and biologics manufacturer. About 77% of revenue is exported (CARE); by geography FY26 revenue was 40% North America, 21% Europe, 23% India and 5% Japan.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** the three businesses deserve different valuations (the street gives CDMO 17-23x EBITDA, CHG 11-15x, PCH 13x EBITDA or 2x sales), but Piramal reports a single segment and no business-level profit. Every segment margin in this report, ours and the street's, is an estimate. That is a real disclosure weakness for a company asking to be valued as a CDMO.

sections.title: History: built by acquisitions, funded by Carlyle and debt, listed in 2022 into a downturn

blocks.p: The Piramal group entered pharma in 1988 with Nicholas Laboratories and sold its Indian branded formulations to Abbott for US$3.7 bn in 2010, keeping contract manufacturing, critical care and consumer brands. In October 2020 Carlyle paid ₹3,523 cr for 20% of the pharma business, money that went into acquisitions (Hemmo peptides, Convergence Chemicals, a stake in Yapan Bio, the Riverview HPAPI site in the US) and capacity. The business was demerged from Piramal Enterprises and listed on 19-Oct-2022, just as post-Covid CDMO demand fell and new overseas capacity came on stream: FY23 EBITDA halved and the stock fell to ~₹65 by March 2023. A ₹1,050 cr rights issue in August 2023 (₹81 a share, promoters subscribing) cut debt. FY24-25 recovered, the September-2024 analyst day set FY30 targets and the stock reached ~₹282, before the FY26 destocking sent it back to ~₹138.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Piramal has never shown a full cycle as a listed company with steady profits; its record is FY23 loss, two near-zero years, FY26 loss. Management guidance missed in FY26 (cut from low single-digit growth to flat; the year ended −3%). That record is why we do not give credit for the FY30 targets in the base case.

sections.title: Industry: CDMO demand is back with biotech money and on-shoring; anaesthesia is mature; Indian OTC grows ~8%

blocks.p: **CDMO.** Global CDMO market ~US$250 bn, growing 7-8% a year (industry estimates in AR FY26 MD&A). US biotech funding rose 30% in FY26 and 75% YoY in H2FY26 (company, industry sources), and 'over 100%' in H1CY26 vs H1CY25 (Q1FY27 presentation). Customers want regulator-grade, multi-site supply outside China; US sites are exempt from US pharma tariffs and UK sites get a nil rate under the UK-US deal, while India's innovation-related work depends on customer negotiations (Chairperson, Q4FY26 call). Competitors have added capacity since the Covid boom and pricing is competitive (CEO, Q4FY26 call).

**ADCs.** Antibody-drug conjugates are among the fastest-growing CDMO niches; Piramal's Grangemouth (UK) site was the world's first USFDA-approved commercial ADC CDMO site; ADC revenue ~US$64 mn in FY26, conjugation is the anchor service (CEO).

**Inhalation anaesthesia.** Global inhalation-anaesthesia market ~US$1 bn; sevoflurane ~84% of it; sevoflurane, isoflurane and desflurane ~81% of the IA market; high entry barriers (dedicated API and drug-product plants, vaporisers, hospital/GPO relationships). Piramal is #1 in US sevoflurane (48% value share, IQVIA) but ex-US markets face Chinese price competition; Piramal answers with lower-cost supply from Digwal.

**Indian consumer health.** Indian OTC market ~US$9 bn, growing ~8% a year to over US$11 bn by 2029 (AR FY26 MD&A); quick commerce is ~50% of Piramal's e-commerce sales; Piramal's consumer business grew about twice its markets in FY26 (Chairperson). **Costs.** The Middle East conflict in 2026 raised sourcing, utility, freight and insurance costs and may force extra inventory; pass-through depends on contracts (CFO, Q4FY26 call).

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the demand tailwind is real and it does reach Piramal, but its value depends on filling the overseas plants that cost the most to run. That makes Piramal a high-operating-leverage play on CDMO demand rather than a steady compounder: if orders convert, margins can rise fast; if they do not, depreciation and interest on the new capacity keep profits near zero.

sections.title: CDMO: a good franchise in development work, an under-filled global plant network, and one customer that showed how fragile commercial supply is

blocks.p: CDMO revenue was ₹5,447 cr in FY25 and ₹4,915 cr in FY26 (−10%). Management blames one "large on-patent commercial product" whose customer ran down excess stock (analysts on the Q4 call called it a migraine drug), weak early-stage orders in H1FY26 and slow biotech funding; excluding the destocked product, CDMO grew modestly and on-patent commercial revenue grew "nearly 50%" across 15-16 products (CEO). Revenue by service in FY26: discovery 2%, development 27%, on-patent commercial manufacturing ~18% (US$96 mn) and other commercial manufacturing 53%. "Differentiated" offerings (ADCs, high-potency APIs, sterile injectables, peptides, on-patent API) rose from 32% of CDMO revenue in FY22 to 44% (US$253 mn) in FY26.

Q1FY27 CDMO revenue rose 19% to ₹1,187 cr, "broad-based across India and overseas sites", with record RFPs, "a number of new logos", a Net Promoter Score of ~60 and margin gains "across most sites". The CFO says ~48% of CDMO revenue comes from overseas sites, whose gross margins are 75-85% against 55-65% in India; at scale EBITDA margins are similar, but today the US and UK plants are sub-scale. No revenue is expected from the destocked product in FY27. Management's FY30 goal is US$1.2 bn of CDMO revenue at ~25% EBITDA margin; FY26 was ~US$555 mn.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the CDMO capability set is genuinely good (ADC conjugation since the early 2000s, a clean regulatory record, an East-West network that big pharma uses), but the business is still mostly commercial supply of mature products plus development work, and its profits depend on filling plants in Lexington, Riverview, Sellersville, Aurora, Grangemouth and Morpeth. Our CDMO revenue of ~US$747 mn in FY29E is well short of management's US$1.2 bn for FY30: we would need to see order conversion, not RFP counts, before we modelled that path.

sections.title: Hospital generics: a cash-generating #1 in US sevoflurane, fighting Chinese prices abroad, with Kenalog as the new lever

blocks.p: CHG revenue was ₹2,633 cr in FY25 and ₹2,703 cr in FY26 (+3%). Inhalation anaesthesia is 64%: Piramal makes sevoflurane API and drug product in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, from a key starting material made in Dahej, and holds 48% of the US sevoflurane market (IQVIA; 45% in Mar-24). Ex-US growth stalled in FY26 under Chinese competition; since FY26 a lower-cost line at Digwal (India) supplies price-sensitive markets (India, UAE, Cambodia, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Uganda, with Bangladesh, Brazil, Malaysia, Russia and South Africa next). Intrathecal therapy (baclofen, morphine; 15%) is #1 in the US and is about defending share; injectable pain (11%) has been limited by a third-party manufacturer's supply problems, with steady supply expected from FY28.

Q1FY27 CHG revenue rose 17% to ₹743 cr on ex-US anaesthesia share gains. Kenalog (triamcinolone acetonide injection), bought from Bristol Myers Squibb for US$35 mn upfront plus up to US$65 mn contingent, starts supplying in Q2FY27; it has limited competition and CHG-like margins. Management describes CHG margins as "stable and will remain stable"; our estimate is ~20% EBITDA before other income in FY26.

sections.title: Consumer healthcare: brands growing 15-24% a year, profits still close to nil after heavy advertising

blocks.p: PCH revenue grew from ₹874 cr in FY23 to ₹1,274 cr in FY26 (+17% in FY26, ~2x its markets). Six "power brands" (Little's, Lacto Calamine, CIR, the i-range and others) grew from ₹370 cr to ₹664 cr (22% a year) and are now 52% of sales; e-commerce grew 48% in FY26 to 27% of sales, half of it through quick commerce. Piramal spends ~12% of PCH sales on media and trade promotion (₹148 cr in FY26). It owns no factories here: production is outsourced. Q1FY27: +15% to ₹347 cr, power brands +23% (53% of sales), e-commerce +40% (28%), price increases to offset input inflation, and a new women's-care master brand (i-choose).

Profitability is the weak point. CARE (17-Jul-2026) says the business's margins "remain in the low single digits", and management talks of margin expansion from premiumisation, fewer but bigger launches and e-commerce profitability rather than of a number. We assume the EBITDA margin rises from ~3% to 7.5% by FY29E.

sections.title: Plants and quality: 17 sites, 49 USFDA inspections since FY12 and no OAI. The quality record is the best part of the CDMO pitch

blocks.p: Piramal runs 15 CDMO sites (nine in India: two in Ahmedabad, Pithampur, Dahej, Digwal, Mahad, Turbhe, Ennore, Rabale R&D; four in North America: Lexington, Riverview, Sellersville, Aurora; two in the UK: Grangemouth and Morpeth), the Bethlehem (US) anaesthesia plant and, through Yapan Bio, a Hyderabad biologics site. Since FY12 it has cleared 415 regulatory inspections including 49 by the USFDA without a single "Official Action Indicated" outcome, and 2,120 customer audits (209 in FY26 alone). Five CDMO sites making ~40% of FY26 CDMO revenue (Digwal, Riverview, Sellersville, Lexington, Aurora) passed USFDA inspections between Sep-2024 and Mar-2026 with zero observations or VAI status; Sellersville received another EIR in Q1FY27.

blocks.p: **Capacity projects.** The US$90 mn US programme adds a commercial payload-linker suite at Riverview (done; "single to low double-digit" US$ mn revenue potential, CEO) and commercial sterile fill-finish at Lexington (104 to 240+ batches a year; H2 CY2027). NewAmsterdam's obicetrapib/ezetimibe suite at Sellersville was customer-funded. CARE notes API sites run at 70-80% utilisation while several formulation sites are under-used; capital turnover (revenue ÷ capital employed) has been 0.60-0.66x since FY22, against 0.74x in FY21.

**The AbbVie JV.** AbbVie Therapeutics India (49%) earned ₹122.9 cr on ₹510 cr of revenue in FY26 (₹140.1 cr in FY25), paid Piramal ₹40.2 cr of dividends and is carried at ₹122.1 cr. Its profit share (₹60.2 cr) is in other income, outside EBITDA, so we value it separately: 5% a year growth gives a Sep-28E share of ~₹68.1 cr, worth ₹681 cr (~₹5.1 a share) at 10x, ICICI Direct's basis. Yapan Bio (33.33%, carrying ₹122 cr) lost money in FY26; we keep it at book.

blocks.callout: **So what:** in a CDMO, a clean regulatory record is a precondition for winning big-pharma commercial supply, and Piramal's is better than most Indian peers'. It reduces one tail risk in our bear case; it does not by itself fill the plants.

sections.title: Moat scorecard: strong in quality and hospital niches, weak in scale and returns

verdicts: 415 inspections incl. 49 by the USFDA since FY12 with no OAI; 209 customer audits in FY26; a rare record among Indian CDMOs and a real selling point for big-pharma work.

#1 in US sevoflurane (48%) with its own API in Bethlehem and KSM in Dahej; #1 in US intrathecal baclofen; Kenalog has limited competition. CHG earns ~20% EBITDA margins (GAM estimate) with stable cash.

Integrated East-West network (13 of the top-20 customers use two or more sites), ADC conjugation at Grangemouth, HPAPI at Riverview, sterile fill-finish at Lexington; but 53% of CDMO revenue is 'other' (generic/off-patent) commercial work and on-patent manufacturing was only US$96 mn in FY26.
Overseas sites are sub-scale: CDMO EBITDA margin is high single digits vs 25-40% at Divi's, Sai Life or Anthem; ROCE 3% in FY26 on ₹8,700 cr of fixed assets.
~500 customers, top-10 36% of CDMO revenue, but one on-patent product's destocking cut FY26 CDMO revenue 10% and swung the group to a loss.
Little's, Lacto Calamine, i-pill and Saridon grow 20%+ with e-commerce at 27-28% of sales, but margins are low single digits after ~12% of sales spent on advertising.
Net debt ₹4,140 cr, 3.6x company EBITDA (4.3x on CARE's basis), above CARE's 3.5x downgrade trigger; more capex and Kenalog payments ahead.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Piramal has narrow moats in two places, its regulatory record and its US hospital niches (sevoflurane, intrathecal baclofen), and neither shows up in group returns because the CDMO plant network is under-filled. In CDMO it competes on capability and reliability against well-funded Indian, Chinese and Western rivals that also added capacity; there is no evidence yet of pricing power (FY26 margins fell with one customer). We would call it a capable operator with a cost and scale problem, not a moat business.

sections.title: Quarters: the March quarter makes the year; Q1 is always the weakest

blocks.p: CDMO customers take delivery late in the fiscal year, so revenue and especially profit bunch in the March quarter: Q4FY25 EBITDA (Screener basis) was ₹561 cr out of ₹1,445 cr for the year (39%), Q4FY26 ₹461 cr out of ₹922 cr (50%). The June quarter is the weakest: Q1FY25 10.5% margin, Q1FY26 5.5%. Q1FY27 revenue was ₹2,270 cr (+17%) with a 8.6% margin (12.5% on the company's basis including other income), a loss of ₹69 cr, and the company says FY27 will again be weighted to the second half. Reading one quarter as a run-rate is the most common mistake with this stock.

blocks.callout: **What to watch:** Q2FY27 (results due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with Kenalog supplies, CDMO order conversion at the overseas sites, and whether management upgrades the "early-to-mid-teens" growth guidance, which it said it would revisit after the September quarter.

sections.title: Five years: revenue up 40%, EBITDA down 35%, profit gone. The overseas build-out and one customer explain most of it

blocks.p: Revenue grew from ₹6,315 cr in FY21 to a peak of ₹9,151 cr in FY25 and slipped to ₹8,869 cr in FY26. EBITDA before other income went the other way: ₹1,428 cr (22.6%) in FY21, a collapse to ₹629 cr (8.9%) in FY23 as Covid-era CDMO orders faded and new overseas plants added fixed cost, a recovery to ₹1,445 cr (15.8%) in FY25, and a second fall to ₹922 cr (10.4%) in FY26 when one large on-patent customer stopped ordering to use up its stock. Below EBITDA the costs of growth kept rising: depreciation from ₹545 cr to ₹831 cr and interest from ₹163 cr to ₹341 cr (peak ₹448 cr in FY24). Net profit fell from ₹835 cr in FY21 to losses in FY23 (₹-186 cr) and FY26 (₹-326 cr), with near-zero profits in between.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Piramal Pharma has spent five years building capacity ahead of demand (₹4,723 cr of capex plus acquisitions), and the return has not come yet: ROCE was 3% in FY26 on Screener's basis. The operating story for FY27 is better (Q1 revenue +17%, EBITDA +72%), but even our FY29E EBITDA of ₹{{F.ebitda.2|num}} cr leaves only ~₹{{F.pat.2|num}} cr of profit after depreciation, interest and a tax bill that runs ahead of profit.

sections.title: Why FY26 turned to a loss: ~₹520 cr of lost operating profit, a tax bill that did not fall with profit, and ₹196 cr of one-offs

blocks.p: Profit went from ₹91 cr in FY25 to a loss of ₹326 cr in FY26, a ₹417 cr swing. Operations: Screener-basis EBITDA fell ₹523 cr (₹1,445 cr to ₹922 cr) as CDMO revenue fell ₹532 cr, mostly the destocked high-margin on-patent product, on a fixed cost base (employee costs +4.7%, other expenses +5.8% incl. a ₹41.8 cr fire loss); other income rose ₹78 cr (forex gains and write-backs). Depreciation rose ₹15 cr; interest fell ₹81 cr (rates and refinancing); the share of associates fell ₹16 cr. Tax fell only ₹174 cr because India profits stay taxed while overseas losses earn no credit. Exceptional items -₹196 cr: impairment of an intangible under development ₹175.8 cr, labour-code gratuity/leave provision ₹26.9 cr, a GBP1.25 mn customer settlement ₹14.8 cr, less a ₹21.4 cr insolvency recovery.

sections.title: Net debt ₹4,140 cr (3.6x company EBITDA, 4.3x on CARE's basis): above the rating trigger, and rising again in FY27

blocks.p: At March 2026 Piramal had ₹5,495 cr of borrowings plus ₹179 cr of leases against ₹1,224 cr of cash and bank balances and ₹132 cr of liquid investments: net debt ₹4,140 cr on the company's basis (₹4,199 cr a year earlier), 3.6x its own EBITDA including other income and 4.5x Screener's EBITDA. Long-term borrowings rose from ₹3,214 cr to ₹4,300 cr in FY26 while short-term debt fell. CARE (AA, Stable, reaffirmed 17-Jul-2026) puts net debt at 4.28x its operating profit, above the 3.5x level it names as a downgrade trigger, and expects it below 3.5x in FY27. Liquidity is fine: ~₹1,332 cr of unencumbered cash and liquid investments, working-capital lines of ₹2,702 cr less than half used, and repayments of ₹630-800 cr a year. Management expects net debt/EBITDA to stay at about 3.6x through FY27 while it spends US$120-135 mn on capex and pays for Kenalog; its long-term goal is ~1x.

Equity has hardly moved: ₹7,911 cr at Mar-24 after the ₹1,050 cr rights issue (Aug-2023, ₹81 a share), ₹8,162 cr at Mar-26, as currency gains on the overseas plants offset the FY26 loss. Working capital is heavy and lumpy: inventory ₹3,064 cr (345 days of material cost on Screener's basis, up from 261) and receivables ₹2,158 cr. FY26 operating cash flow of ₹1,653 cr was flattered by ₹945 cr more payables; management warns some of that may reverse.

sections.title: Capital allocation: ₹4,700 cr of capex and ₹1,000 cr of acquisitions in six years for a 3% return on capital

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Piramal generated ₹5,398 cr of operating cash and spent ₹4,723 cr on fixed assets and ₹1,002 cr on acquisitions (FY21-22), funded by Carlyle's ₹3,523 cr (FY21), the ₹1,050 cr rights issue (FY24) and debt. ROCE on Screener's basis was 7% in FY22, 2% in FY23, 5-6% in FY24-25 and 3% in FY26, against a cost of capital of ~12%. FY27 capex is guided at US$120-135 mn plus Kenalog; management says growth capex continues after Lexington. Its FY30 goals include a high-teens ROCE and net debt/EBITDA of ~1x; on our numbers ROE reaches only {{F.roe.2|pct}} in FY29E.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** management has built the plants; the next three years are about filling them. We would judge capital allocation on two numbers: whether FY27-28 capex falls towards maintenance levels as CARE expects, and whether net debt starts falling from FY28. Further acquisitions like Kenalog (small, accretive, already on the market) are fine; a large one before the existing capacity earns its keep would not be.

sections.title: Ownership: Piramal family 34.8%, Carlyle ~18% and looking for the exit, domestic funds ~15%

blocks.p: At June 2026 the Piramal family held 34.8% (34.85% at Mar-26; it subscribed to the 2023 rights issue and has not pledged shares). The largest outside holder is CA Alchemy Investments, a Carlyle affiliate, with 17.95% (23.87 cr shares at Mar-26), the remainder of the 20% bought for ₹3,523 cr in October 2020. Carlyle has twice prepared to sell: a ~10% block was reported in July 2025, and a 6-10% sell-down (₹1,750-2,700 cr) was reported cancelled on 14-Aug-2026 (IFR). At Mar-26, mutual funds held 14.12%, other foreign portfolio investors 12.23%, insurers 1.24% and individuals ~14%. Screener's Jun-2026 categories move 17.7pp from 'FIIs' to 'public' with no matching trade; the size matches CA Alchemy's 17.95%, which the company classes as foreign direct investment rather than portfolio investment. We could not open the Jun-2026 BSE filing (HTTP 403), so we treat Carlyle's stake as unchanged.

blocks.p: House rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): the stock's own one-year-forward multiple (EV ÷ next full year's EBITDA) over its window, leaving out trough years (tested on forward EBITDA for an EV/EBITDA history), times the sector factor over the same window, rounded to the half-turn. Piramal listed in October 2022, so its window starts on 1-May-2023 (post-listing months skipped) and pairs with the nine pharma peers' move since then. Piramal reports one segment, so the three businesses take one multiple; the street's segment multiples are sensitivity rows. No blend with Piramal's own re-rating and no growth uplift.

The market prices Piramal on EBITDA and on the FY30 margin goal; the cash flows do not yet justify today's price. That is the main risk to the stock, and the reason our bear case is so far below.

blocks.p: Even with management's long-run tax rate and margin goal the DCF (₹156) stays below the ₹207 price. The reasons are structural: heavy working capital (~27% of sales on Screener's balance sheet), capex that stays at 8-15% of sales through FY27-29E, and depreciation on plants that are not yet full. A cash-flow investor needs margins well above 25% or a much lower cost of capital to pay today's price; an EV/EBITDA investor needs only the history to repeat. sections.title: Our honest summary: upside on the multiple the market has paid for Piramal, but a stock for those who can live with thin profits and high debt

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a global CDMO with a rare regulatory record, ADC and high-potency capabilities and under-used plants in the US and UK that could earn a lot if filled; the US leader in inhaled anaesthetics with a new acquired brand (Kenalog); a fast-growing but barely profitable Indian consumer business; 49% of a profitable eye-care JV with AbbVie; and ₹4,140 cr of net debt. Revenue is growing again (+17% in Q1FY27) and we expect EBITDA to rise ~60% by FY28E.

**What you are paying:** ₹207 is ~15.7x our Sep-28E EBITDA after net debt and the JV, 89.0x FY28E EPS, after a ~19% rise in 2026. Our 21x is Piramal's own forward median since May-2023 (20.0x, every weekly point), lifted 5.1% for a sector trading above its history: {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). Earnings-based and cash-flow checks are much lower (P/E ₹119, DCF ₹98).

blocks.p: **Why BUY, and how confident are we?** The rule compares the price with a target built on the street's method (a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA) at the multiple Piramal itself has traded on since May-2023, and on our recovery numbers that is ~36% above the price. We do not need the bulls' margins for it: ICICI Direct's 16-18% path would add another ~₹40-60 a share. But the call rests on the market paying its historical multiple again. That history includes Apr-24 to Mar-25, when EV/EBITDA reached ~33x on collapsing EBITDA; without those dates the target would be ₹205 (HOLD), and on earnings (₹119) or cash flows (₹98) the stock looks expensive. **What would change our mind:** H2FY27 margins below ~12% (orders not converting), another customer destocking, or a CARE downgrade on leverage.
